items.evidence: python roll.py --headless --ticks N --script "T:word,..." [--board B] [--settings DIR] runs with no window and prints one JSON object with tick, screen, board, score, lives, ball, coins, crates, bridge_x, volume, language, selected, texts, sounds (plus an extra quit key).
Adding --frame out.png wrote a valid PNG for every run I tried (15 frames: title, settings, play boards 1-3, paused, won, lost in en and es). The IHDR header says 800 x 480 for each.

sounds/*.wav and `python roll.py --wav NAME out.wav` both give coin 0.36 s, bounce 0.16 s, fall 0.80 s, clear 0.84 s. Each has peak above 21000, and all four have different data hashes and zero-crossing rates (2489, 250, 790, 1645 per s).

Tick 0: screen title, selected Start. menu_down gives Settings, then Quit, then wraps to Start; menu_up from Start gives Quit. Script 0:enter gives screen play, board 1, score 0, lives 3, texts [Board 1 of 3, Score: 0, Lives: 3].

Settings at first shows texts [Settings, Volume: 8, Language: English, Back]. One menu_right gives 9; 12 menu_left give 0; 6 menu_right give 10 (clamped). On Language, menu_right and menu_left both switch to es. Choosing Back gives screen title.

Settings folder set to es. Title: Roll/Iniciar/Ajustes/Salir. Settings: Ajustes/Volumen: 8/Idioma: Español/Volver. Play: Tablero 1 de 3/Puntos: 0/Vidas: 3. Paused adds En pausa/Continuar/Salir al título. Won: ¡Has ganado!/Puntos: 30/Pulsa Intro... Lost: Fin del juego. No English left (only the name Roll).

In a run with --settings set1 I set volume 3 and es. A second run with the same folder started at volume 3 and es, and set1/settings.json holds {volume:3, language:es}. A run with no --settings started at 8 and en.
Board 1 with no input: y first <= 0.3 at tick 26 and back above 0.3 at tick 29. After 600 ticks y = 0.25 exactly, and sounds has bounce 3 times.

Board 1, push for ticks 100-130 then none. right: x 0 to 0.499, then 1.43 at tick 160 and 2.47 at 200. left: -x. up: -z. down: +z (same magnitudes). After the push ends, velocity is still 1.50 m/s along the push after 70 ticks.

Board 1 driven script: each coin adds exactly 10 (0 to 10 to 20 to 30 to 40), the coin leaves coins, and coin is appended to sounds. On the 4th coin (tick 512): board 2, clear in sounds, ball at (-3, 1.25, 0) with zero velocity, the 3 board-2 coins, and 6 crates.
--board 2 with no input: crates at (0, 0.25 or 0.75, -0.5/0/0.5). Their largest distance from home over 300 ticks is 0.0000 (y 0.24999), and the ball rests at (-3, 0.25, 0).

--board 2, 60:right (held): the bottom-middle crate is shoved off the board and removed, and the top-middle crate drops to the floor and ends at (0.37, 0.25, 0); with 60:right,150:none it is 0.8 m from home. The ball reaches x=1 at tick 160, against tick 149 on the same board with no crates. No crate was ever below y 0.2 while over the board.
--board 2, 60:right,150:none: a crate is pushed along x to 4.05 (tick 241), falls (y -1.28 at 271, -4.90 at 299 with x 5.15), and is gone from crates at tick 300 (6 to 5). The other 5 remain.

Board 2 fall at tick 327: lives 3 to 2, fall appended, ball reset to (-3, 1.25, 0) and then dropped to rest. Coins before and after are identical, crates before and after are identical (one displaced at x 0.366), and score stays 10. A run losing a life on board 1 (lives 2) then clearing it reaches board 2 with lives 2, and a later fall gives 1.
--board 3 with no input: bridge_x at ticks 90/180/270/360 is 1.0/2.0/1.0/0.0, repeating at 450/540/630/720 as 1/2/1/0.

--board 3, 234:right,298:left,362:none: the ball comes to rest on the bridge (on_bridge) by tick 392. Over the next 400 ticks (through a reversal) |x - bridge_x| <= 0.251, y stays 0.25 and no life is lost. With 60:right the ball reaches the edge while bridge_x is ~1.4, drops through the gap and loses a life at tick 201.

--board 3 --script 0:right: coins taken at -2, then (1,0) from the bridge, then 5. At tick 130: screen won, score 30, sounds ending in clear. At tick 400, with left and menu_down added in between, the state is identical. 400:enter gives screen title.

--board 1 --script 0:right: after 3 falls screen is lost by tick 410 (lives 0, score 10). Adding left/up/none pushes and running to tick 710 gives identical score, ball, coins and crates. Enter gives screen title.

Board 3 (escape at 100) and board 2 mid-strike (escape at 160): screen paused, and after 200 more ticks the ball, crates, bridge_x and score are byte-identical. Enter on Resume returns to play and motion continues. menu_down+enter (Quit to title) gives screen title.
Two CLI runs of --board 2 --ticks 400 --script 60:right,150:none printed identical JSON, including the displaced crate at x 0.3660350624988501.

Board 2 frames show a perspective view from above and +z with the whole slab, a red ball with highlight and shadow at the state position, brown boxes with distinct top and side shading where the state puts them (also after a strike), and the uncollected coins. Board 3 frames show two slabs, the gap, and the bridge centred in the gap at bridge_x=1 and touching the right slab at 2.

Viewed the PNGs: the Spanish title, settings, paused, won and lost frames show the Spanish texts (as the font's uppercase), and the English ones show English. The play frames show BOARD n OF 3 / SCORE / LIVES (TABLERO n DE 3 / PUNTOS / VIDAS in es).

sound.wav_bytes scales the samples by volume/10; at --volume 0 all four WAVs have peak 0. gui.py:170 plays only when game.volume > 0 and passes the volume to wav_bytes. The headless sounds list is still filled at any volume.
README gives the play keys and goal, the exact headless, frame and wav commands (all worked as written), and a Files section saying what each file holds.

defects: Crates never rotate. In the strike only the middle column moves: the bottom crate is bulldozed ahead of the ball and the top one drops straight down. Crates never topple, as the README admits.

Ground support is tested only at the ball's centre, and a ball up to 0.3 below the top surface (y > -0.05) is snapped back on top. A bouncing ball can therefore cross a 0.5 m gap to the bridge and pop up through its side (board 3 with 0:right clears without the bridge needing to be adjacent).
The bitmap font is uppercase only, so the frames show texts in capitals rather than exactly as in texts.
Ball-to-board landing only checks the centre, so a ball whose centre is just past an edge drops through, though its body overlaps the slab.

trace.how: context, new, read_again and how far the context grew are the run's own records. written_out a request is its growth less its answers (characters / 4), scaled to the run's exact total; of_which_unseen is that less the visible text (thinking). cost is what the request read and wrote, weighted; carried is what reading again what it added cost at every later request (start.carried: the same for what every request starts from). reading + writing is in_the_ledger
